(2) Nyengaard's "house of cards" quote is also absent from GT -- a direct authorial characterization of the discovery as a paradigm shift, not incremental confirmation, which GT never articulates this way. Standard tier, since it conveys a perspective rather than a new fact. The comparative-structures candidate remains classified under breadth, not depth (see below).

**1:** [instances=2; quality=standard,standard] (1) Coen Elemans' quote ("This pecten allows a snake eagle the incredible acuity of vision to spot a tiny still lizard from great heights...") is not paraphrased or indirectly quoted anywhere in GT -- GT's own vision-enables-hunting examples are owl/albatross/hummingbird, a different specific illustration. A direct, vivid, on-the-record example from a named contributor that GT doesn't include is new content in its own right. (2) Dan-Eric Nilsson's corroboration quote ("I fully support their interpretation that the anoxic retina probably evolved in the dinosaur lineage") is also absent from GT. Per ruling, this counts as valuable in its own right: quoting an independent, established scholar (a sensory biologist not involved in the research) for external validation is a distinct journalistic function -- credibility/corroboration from an outside authority -- separate from whether the quote's specific wording carries a new fact. Both standard tier. The clinical-stroke-classification and retinal-damage-pathology candidates remain classified under breadth (see below); the exaptation/high-altitude claim still restates content GT already covers via Damsgaard's own speculation, so it remains uncredited.
